text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet meeting adopts draft electoral law to provide Morocco with legislation to ensure transparent polls.
- The European Union granted Morocco $138.3 million for social and financial structural adjustment to help its moves towards setting up a free trade zone with the EU.
- Crown Prince Mohamed inaugurates bypass linking Rabat and twin city of Sale.
- Spanish Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio's visit accompanied by a strong fisheries team shows fishing arrangements are top of the agenda.
- Fire in mill in central city of Sidi Slimane kills two, injures six and causes severe damage.
- More than 25,000 people attended burial in Tangier of Moroccan Loubna Benaissa, killed in Belgium.
- Consumption of coffee might decrease following cost rises triggered by increases in international markets.

- Trade ministry and U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) set up association in central city of Fez to grant loans to craftsmen and small traders from 1,000 dirhams ($106) to 10,000 dirhams without asking them for guarantees.
